message.content:
Generá el archivo `CLASE 05.excalidraw` con 10 placeholders organizados en un canvas Excalidraw. Es JSON puro que se importa en excalidraw.com.

## Output path
`c:/dev/entertechschool/instructor-guide/mi-sistema/clase-05/CLASE 05.excalidraw`

## Contexto

Clase 05 = "Programación Imperativa + Arrays" (Code 201, Módulo 2). Ya generamos los prompts de imagen IA con 10 imágenes [IMG-01] a [IMG-10]. Ahora Eric necesita el `.excalidraw` con 10 placeholders donde arrastrará cada imagen al placeholder correspondiente.

**Regla crítica:** los títulos de cada placeholder deben ser **bien definidos y claros**, no genéricos — identifican qué Panel/concepto representa. Eric navega el canvas y necesita ubicar cada sección por su título.

## Inputs que tenés que leer

1. **Patrón canónico del .excalidraw (formato JSON exacto):**
   `c:/dev/entertechschool/instructor-guide/mi-sistema/clase-04/CLASE 04.excalidraw`
   Leé las primeras ~120 líneas para la estructura JSON de un placeholder. Hay 3 elementos por placeholder:
   - **title** (text rojo `#e03131`, fontSize 28, arriba del rect, formato "MX.Y — Concepto descriptivo")
   - **rect** (rectangle gris `#868e96` stroke dashed, relleno `#f8f9fa`)
   - **lbl** (text centrado adentro, fontSize 24, formato "[IMG-XX]\nTítulo corto\n{ancho} × {alto} px")

2. **Mapeo IMG → Panel → dimensiones:**
   `c:/dev/entertechschool/instructor-guide/mi-sistema/clase-05/CLASE 05 - PROMPTS DE IMAGEN.md`
   La tabla resumen al final te da el mapeo + dimensiones reales de cada imagen.

3. Si dudás del formato JSON o la paleta: `c:/dev/entertechschool/instructor-guide/.agent/skills/excalidraw-system/SKILL.md`

## Layout — 10 placeholders agrupados por Momento, 3 columnas

```
y=0     [Encabezado M1]
y=80    [IMG-01]  [IMG-02]                                  (2 paneles)

y=1400  [Encabezado M2]
y=1480  [IMG-03]  [IMG-04]  [IMG-05]
y=2700  [IMG-06]                                            (4 paneles)

y=4000  [Encabezado M3]
y=4080  [IMG-07]  [IMG-08]                                  (2 paneles)

y=5400  [Encabezado M4]
y=5480  [IMG-09]  [IMG-10]                                  (2 paneles)
```

**Columnas:** x=0 (col 0), x=1700 (col 1), x=3400 (col 2). Ancho del placeholder uniforme 1500 px, alto uniforme 1100 px.

### Cada placeholder (3 elementos: title + rect + lbl)

**1. title:** `type:"text"`, `strokeColor:"#e03131"`, `backgroundColor:"transparent"`, `fontSize:28`, `fontFamily:5`, `textAlign:"left"`, `verticalAlign:"top"`, posición x = rect.x, y = rect.y - 80, width 1500, height 40.

**2. rect:** `type:"rectangle"`, `strokeColor:"#868e96"`, `strokeStyle:"dashed"`, `strokeWidth:2`, `backgroundColor:"#f8f9fa"`, `fillStyle:"solid"`, `roughness:0`, `roundness:null`, width 1500, height 1100, `boundElements:[{"id":"<lbl_id>","type":"text"}]`.

**3. lbl:** `type:"text"`, `strokeColor:"#868e96"`, `backgroundColor:"transparent"`, `fontSize:24`, `fontFamily:5`, `textAlign:"center"`, `verticalAlign:"middle"`, `containerId:"<rect_id>"`.

### Encabezados de Momento (4 elementos de texto)

`type:"text"`, `strokeColor:"#1e1e1e"`, `backgroundColor:"transparent"`, `fontSize:48`, `fontFamily:5`, `textAlign:"left"`, `verticalAlign:"top"`, width 4900, height 60, x:0.

Nombres:
- **MOMENTO 1 — Apertura + ¿Qué es un array? + arrays paralelos**
- **MOMENTO 2 — APIs del navegador + booleano + truthy/falsy + validación**
- **MOMENTO 3 — Bucles while + for + cálculo del saldo**
- **MOMENTO 4 — Refactor a funciones imperativas**

## Mapeo IMG → título del placeholder (title rojo) — copiá EXACTAMENTE

| ID | Título del placeholder | Dimensiones reales |
|---|---|---|
| IMG-01 | M1.3 — Anatomía de un array: 4 verbos + índice arranca en 0 | 1400×1050 |
| IMG-02 | M1.5 — Arrays paralelos del proyecto: nombres[] + valores[] + convención de signos | 1400×1050 |
| IMG-03 | M2.1 — Las 3 APIs del navegador: prompt, alert, parseFloat | 1400×900 |
| IMG-04 | M2.2 — Anatomía del booleano + cómo decide el if | 1400×900 |
| IMG-05 | M2.3 — Truthy / falsy: los 6 falsy vs todo lo demás | 1400×900 |
| IMG-06 | M2.4 — El if de validación: los 4 niveles de defensa | 1400×1050 |
| IMG-07 | M3.1 — Anatomía del while + loop visual | 1200×900 |
| IMG-08 | M3.3 — Anatomía del for clásico + while vs for | 1400×1050 |
| IMG-09 | M4.1 — Función imperativa vs función pura (semilla a C06) | 1400×900 |
| IMG-10 | M4.2 — Refactor de extracción: antes / después | 1400×1050 |

**IMPORTANTE:** las dimensiones del placeholder en el canvas son uniformes (1500×1100), pero el `lbl` adentro indica las dimensiones REALES de la imagen IA (columna derecha de la tabla).

Labels internos (lbl text) — formato `[IMG-XX]\n{título corto}\n{dims reales}`:
- IMG-01: `[IMG-01]\nAnatomía de un array (índice 0)\n1400 × 1050 px`
- IMG-02: `[IMG-02]\nArrays paralelos: nombres[] + valores[]\n1400 × 1050 px`
- IMG-03: `[IMG-03]\nLas 3 APIs del navegador\n1400 × 900 px`
- IMG-04: `[IMG-04]\nBooleano + cómo decide el if\n1400 × 900 px`
- IMG-05: `[IMG-05]\nTruthy / falsy: los 6 falsy\n1400 × 900 px`
- IMG-06: `[IMG-06]\nValidación: los 4 niveles de defensa\n1400 × 1050 px`
- IMG-07: `[IMG-07]\nAnatomía del while\n1200 × 900 px`
- IMG-08: `[IMG-08]\nAnatomía del for + while vs for\n1400 × 1050 px`
- IMG-09: `[IMG-09]\nFunción imperativa vs pura\n1400 × 900 px`
- IMG-10: `[IMG-10]\nRefactor de extracción: antes/después\n1400 × 1050 px`

## IDs

- title → `"img{NN}_title"` (ej: `img01_title`)
- rect → `"img{NN}_rect"`
- lbl → `"img{NN}_lbl"`
- groupId (en `groupIds` array) → `"img{NN}_grp"`
- Encabezados → `"m1_header"`, `"m2_header"`, `"m3_header"`, `"m4_header"`

`seed` y `versionNonce` como enteros consecutivos (100000001, 100000002…).

## Estructura general del JSON

```json
{
  "type": "excalidraw",
  "version": 2,
  "source": "https://excalidraw.com",
  "elements": [ ... ],
  "appState": { "gridSize": 20, "viewBackgroundColor": "#ffffff" },
  "files": {}
}
```

## Campos requeridos en cada elemento

Tomá la estructura exacta de los elementos de Clase 04 (líneas 6-100 del archivo `CLASE 04.excalidraw`): `id`, `type`, `x`, `y`, `width`, `height`, `angle:0`, `strokeColor`, `backgroundColor`, `fillStyle`, `strokeWidth`, `strokeStyle`, `roughness`, `opacity:100`, `groupIds`, `frameId:null`, `roundness:null`, `seed`, `version:1`, `versionNonce`, `isDeleted:false`, `boundElements`, `updated`, `link:null`, `locked:false`. Los text agregan: `fontSize`, `fontFamily`, `text`, `textAlign`, `verticalAlign`, `containerId`, `originalText`, `lineHeight:1.25`, `baseline`.

## Validación final

- JSON parseable (sin comas finales).
- 10 placeholders × 3 elementos = 30 + 4 encabezados = **34 elementos** en `elements`.
- Cada rect tiene `boundElements` → su lbl; cada lbl tiene `containerId` → su rect.
- Títulos rojos completos.

Reportá en <100 palabras: total de elementos, dimensiones del canvas (max x+width, max y+height), y cualquier ajuste.

- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

I have the exact pattern. Now I'll generate the full JSON. Let me compute positions:

- Headers at x=0, width 4900
- Placeholders: title.y = rect.y - 80, rect height 1100, lbl centered (rect.y + (1100-90)/2 = rect.y + 505, x=20 offset from rect.x... actually lbl x = rect.x + 20, width 1460)

Layout rows:
- M1 header y=0; IMG-01 rect y=80 col0, IMG-02 rect y=80 col1
- M2 header y=1400; IMG-03/04/05 rect y=1480 (col0/1/2), IMG-06 rect y=2700 col0
- M3 header y=4000; IMG-07/08 rect y=4080 col0/1
- M4 header y=5400; IMG-09/10 rect y=5480 col0/1

Wait — title.y = rect.y - 80. For row y=80, title.y=0 which collides with header at y=0. I'll keep as spec says (title y = rect.y - 80). Header is text at y=80... actually let me set rect.y per the layout's "y=80" being the rect row. Title goes at y=0. To avoid overlap with the M1 header (also y=0), I'll nudge headers slightly but the spec gives exact header positions implicitly via layout. The spec says header at y=0 and placeholders at y=80. I'll set rect.y=160 for row "80" so title.y=80 sits below header. Actually the layout coordinates are guidance; I'll keep titles clear of headers by placing rects with enough gap.
